title: Ordinary finite reduction of signed point section modules
statement: For a finite-field datum and prime different from its characteristic, the ordinary coefficient tensor of each integral signed section module with every positive integer-ring quotient is isomorphic to the corresponding finite signed section module [def-pur-point-tate-comparison-data]. On every pure tensor a tensor x its map is a times the evaluation of the fixed signed reduction of x; the latter is the unique reduction family of [lem-weil-signed-twist-reduction-comparison].

source.place: Finite-reduction sentence; coefficient comparison lemma step 2, sections-tensor isomorphism only.

proof.text: choose compatible primitive roots and use point_tate_root_coordinates to trivialize the integral and residue signed sheaves. In these coordinates the normalized reduction sends c times the integral generator to its residue times the finite generator. In degree zero this is the coefficient quotient; in degree one it is the defining root tensor quotient; tensor induction proves it for positive degrees. For a negative degree evaluate the dual comparison on the positive basis, giving the same coefficient quotient by the signed reduction normalization. Evaluation at the terminal object identifies the two coefficient units with the actual integer ring and its positive quotient. The induced map on a tensor a tensor (c times the integral generator) is a times residue(c) times the residue generator. Its inverse sends a times the residue generator to  a tensor the integral generator. Tensor balancing proves the inverse equations for arbitrary quotient rings; no reducedness or field property is used. The resulting isomorphism is independent of the root basis, because its pure-tensor formula refers to the fixed reduction map and pure tensors generate.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteSectionComparison (hl : l ≠ D.p) :
    ∃ z : FiniteComparisons D l,
    (∀ (F : Type u) [Field F] [Algebra (Padic l) F]
        [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) F] (n : ℕ) (m : ℤ)
        (a : Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l F (n + 1)) (x : integral D l F m),
      (z F n m).hom (a ⊗ₜ[Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l F,
          Ideal.Quotient.mk (Padic.coefficientExtensionIdeal l F (n + 1))] x) =
        a • (@id (finite D l F n m)
          ((reduction D l F hl n m).val.app (finalObject D) x)))
